name: White-bearded Greenbul
rangeDescription: Southeastern nigeria and cameroon to gabon, angola, and northern democratic republic of the congo
description: A medium-sized greenbul often found in flocks in forest and forest edge with other bearded-greenbuls. Like all bearded-greenbuls, will sometimes puff out throat feathers.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Northern Gannet
rangeDescription: Breeds north atlantic coasts; ranges to coastal northwestern africa
description: Large seabird of the Atlantic with long, pointed bill, wings, and tail. Adults bright white with cream-colored head and black wingtips.

name: Pacific Tuftedcheek
rangeDescription: West slope of western andes of southwestern colombia and western ecuador
description: Handsome arboreal bird restricted to wet cloud forest in the western Andes. Its conspicuous neck tufts are often tinged with buff and can be flared out if the bird is excited or agitated.

name: Stresemann's Bush-Crow
rangeDescription: Southern ethiopia (sidamo province)
description: An unusual small crow-like bird with gray, black, and white plumage. There is bright blue bare skin around the eye, and sometimes a small pink patch is also visible behind the eye.

name: Black-capped Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Mountains of costa rica and western panama
description: Small flycatcher, darker than other similar species, with particularly noteworthy black cap and teardrop-shaped white eyering. Dull brownish wingbars.

name: Venezuelan Bristle-Tyrant
rangeDescription: Coastal cordillera of northern venezuela (carabobo to distrito federal)
description: Small olive-yellow flycatcher with black ear patch, gray crown, pinkish lower mandible, and bold, contrasting yellowish wing bars. Sexes similar.

name: Yucatan Poorwill
rangeDescription: Southern mexico (yucatán peninsula) to northern belize and petén of northern guatemala
description: Small dark nightjar of humid lowland forest in the Yucatan Peninsula, heard far more often than seen. Favors dense tangled forest, less often edges, and usually sings from a concealed perch.

name: Hartlaub's Turaco
rangeDescription: Highlands of kenya, adjacent uganda, and northeastern tanzania
description: A beautiful green turaco with dark blue wings, tail, and crown. Note the white markings on the head: a white spot in front of the eye and a white line below the eye.

name: Yellow-bellied Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: Humid lowlands of southern mexico (oaxaca) to northeastern costa rica
description: A tiny, stub-tailed flycatcher of humid tropical forest. Spends most of its time in the canopy, where overlooked easily, but at times descends lower, mainly at forest edges.

name: Gyrfalcon
rangeDescription: Mountains and tundra of northern palearctic region and northern north america
description: Stocky beast of a falcon; ranges in color from strikingly white to silvery-gray to dark sooty-brown. Relatively long tail and broad wings with powerful flight.

name: Cuban Bullfinch
rangeDescription: Cuba including isla de la juventud (isle of pines; south of western cuba)
description: Endemic to Cuba. A small flocking species of brushy and wooded habitats.

name: Green-breasted Mountain-gem
rangeDescription: Humid montane forest of eastern honduras and north-central nicaragua
description: Medium-sized hummingbird, not particularly bright. Green above and dingy grayish below with dense green spots on sides and breast.

name: Meratus White-eye
rangeDescription: Meratus mountains, south kalimantan, southeastern borneo
description: A recently described species from montane rainforest in SE Borneo. Overall olive-green with a brighter yellow throat, undertail and belly stripe.

name: Temminck's Tragopan
rangeDescription: Hill and montane forest of northeastern india to central china (zhejiang southward through guangxi), northern myanmar, and northwestern tonkin
description: Rotund terrestrial bird of hilly forests, usually seen singly. Male exquisitely colored: bright flame-orange overall, with white dots all over the body, black face, and electric blue facial wattle that is inflated into a liver-shaped, dazzling red-and-blue flap during courtship.

name: Northern Shrike-tit
rangeDescription: Northern australia (kimberley to arnhem land and far northwestern queensland)
description: Small bird with short, heavy bill. Green above, yellow below, with bold black-and-white head pattern.

name: Kakapo
rangeDescription: Now mostly codfish island (=whenua hou, west of stewart island); formerly north, south, and stewart islands (new zealand); extremely rare and intensively managed
description: New Zealand’s largest endemic parrot. Flightless, nocturnal, and solitary, confined to several predator-free offshore islands.

name: Purple-capped Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Caroline islands (chuuk and pohnpei)
description: Colorful forest dove found solely on the Caroline Islands of Chuuk and Pohnpei; the only fruit-dove on these islands. Adult has a bright purple cap, leaf-green back and wings, and a broad lemon-yellow tail tip.

name: Yellow-throated Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Southeastern assam (manipur and lushai hills) to western myanmar
description: A small, slim laughingthrush with an obvious yellow belly and black mask. Similar to Rufous-vented Laughingthrush, but the Yellow-throated Laughingthrush is smaller, with a smaller bill and a whitish vent and undertail.

name: Ultramarine Kingfisher
rangeDescription: Eastern and central solomon islands
description: A distinctive medium-sized blue-and-white kingfisher with a prominent dark mask, blue crown, bright white neck and underparts, blue wings and back, and reddish undertail. Male has a white rump.
imageCreditName: Lars Petersson | My World of Bird Photography

name: Necklaced Barbet
rangeDescription: Mountains of eastern laos and southern vietnam
description: Brightly-colored barbet restricted to the Annamite Range of southern Vietnam and southeastern Laos, where it inhabits hill and montane forests. Like other barbets, often sticks close to dense foliage in the canopy, where it can be difficult to see; listen instead for its echoing hiccuping song, which has a frog-like quality.
